topic: Thread Management Burden: Avoiding Oversubscription and Exhaustion
explanation: Programming directly with `std::thread` forces the developer to assume the burden of dealing with thread exhaustion, CPU oversubscription (creating more threads than hardware cores), and manual load balancing. This complexity is typically handled automatically and more efficiently by the underlying system when using task-based abstractions like `std::async`.
practical_example: A legacy system using raw `std::thread` creation fails frequently under heavy load because it creates hundreds of threads, leading to resource exhaustion and excessive context switching overhead, problems that a task-based approach would mitigate.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
